I stopped this review as **BLOCKED** before reviewing anything, because the candidate-identity precondition failed. I raised no findings and wrote no verifications file, so F-DG5-102 stays **OPEN**.

**The mismatch:**
- **The frozen commit is fine.** `fb9c221` still produces the assigned ID, `sha256:26d4ad92…e1bf` (2188 files). I checked it with `--ref fb9c221` and with a complete, non-shallow clone checked out at `fb9c221`.
- **HEAD is a different tree.** HEAD `dc4364c` produces `sha256:9ac47c24…3814` in the repository, with `--ref HEAD`, and in a full clone. `--diff` against the frozen manifest exits 1 with one changed file: `tools/agents/agent_settings.py`.
- **The cause is the D-176 commit.** `738831e` added `"allowNestedUserNamespaces": True` to the agents' Bash sandbox settings after the freeze, without a re-freeze. `tools/agents/**` is inside the candidate spec, which includes every path.

**Why it blocks:**
- My agent definition says to stop and return BLOCKED when the recomputed ID differs.
- The normal (non-historical) gate check recomputes the ID from the working tree and rejects a mismatch (`tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:985-999`). So a DG5 gate on `26d4ad…` cannot pass at this HEAD, whatever any review says.
- The change loosens the reviewers' own sandbox, which is security-relevant tooling in my remit, and no review round has covered it. I did not judge it on its merits.
- D-176 appears only in the assignment files and the commit message; `docs/delivery/decisions.md` has no D-176 entry.

**Not run (none of it counts as PASS):** the F-DG5-102 re-check, the repair-diff and P5 diff reviews, the static checks, the Node 22 and Node 24 unit runs, both integration runs, and `validate --historical`.

**To unblock, either:**
- (a) record D-176 in `decisions.md`, re-freeze DG5 at a commit that includes it (a new candidate ID), and reissue the round-4 assignments; or
- (b) restore the HEAD tree so it hashes to `26d4ad…` again, if the runner setting can be applied without changing tracked files.

**Leftover file:** `docs/delivery/reviews/DG5/round-4/code-security-reviewer.verifications.json` from the earlier R4C run is still there. I couldn't remove it because I can only write my own new files. This run wrote no verifications file, so you will need to deal with that one when you reissue.

Files are in `docs/delivery/`:
- `reviews/DG5/round-4/code-security-reviewer.json` (verdict BLOCKED, all 42 requirement IDs listed, no findings)
- `test-evidence/DG5/code-security/round-4/r4d-00-candidate-identity.log`

The two clones are deleted.
